expert: Ghostwriting agency owner (8 founder/exec accounts on X + LinkedIn, would buy Studio)

typefully-a.verdict: The only page that names me in the first screen ('For ghostwriters' in the nav) and then shows the per-client approval queue I actually run, but makes me scroll 7 screens to reach it.
typefully-a.loved: The client switcher: each client (Priya, Rafael, Lena, Marco) gets a different voice ('Lowercase, chart first, says when he was wrong'), a never-say list, time zone and best slot, and an approvals line like '3 posts waiting on Marco / 2 approved, scheduled by you'. Pair that with the review link line 'no account needed', which matters because my founders will never make an account, and it replaces my Typefully + Docs + Slack loop on one screen.
problems: Headline says 'Six clients. Six voices.' but the switcher lists four clients. I count accounts for a living, so I notice, and so would a client I show this to.
The Studio section sits at about 7.0 desktop screens and 10.7 phone screens, below Results, Pays, Who and every solo feature; the nav link is doing all the work.
The 'Your data →' link under 'It drafts. You press send.' points to #privacy, which doesn't exist. That's the one trust link an agency would click.
Review links (with client comments on exact words) live in the features grid, not inside the Studio panel, so the client-comment, approve and schedule loop never appears as one flow.
typefully-a.fix: Move the Studio block up to directly after Sharpen and add a 'Review link' tab inside the client panel showing that client's comment and an Approve, so the whole loop shows for one client. Also fix 'Six clients' to match the list.

apple-b.verdict: The best single Studio screenshot of the five (review link, client comment, never-say and Approve in one app frame) under a headline I can't miss, but the first screen and the pricing still read as solo-first.
apple-b.loved: The 'Your clients. Their voices.' app mock: client list with time zones (PST, GMT+1, SGT), a draft marked 'review link shared', an editor note 'via review link', the client saying 'Love it. Ship Tuesday.', a voice line, never-say chips (synergy, thrilled to announce, disrupt) and 'Waiting on Dev · Tue 8:40 AM' with Approve. That's the exact screen I'd forward to a prospective client.
problems: The only first-screen hint is a nav item called 'Studio', which means nothing to a stranger. The hero, 'Write the line they stop for' over a drifting feed, is pure solo creator.
It isn't clear who presses Approve: me, or the client through the review link. That's the exact question my clients ask, and the client's side of the review link is never shown.

In the default pricing view Studio says only '$18 per client voice, a month / Billed yearly.' The $24 monthly price is hidden until you toggle, and Free gets the filled CTA while 'Choose Studio' is a ghost button.
On phone the client list collapses to just Dev Raman, so the 'many clients, many voices' point disappears.
apple-b.fix: Rename the nav item 'For ghostwriters', and in the mock label the approval step from the client's side ('Dev approved via review link · no account'). Show '$24 billed monthly' under Studio in both toggle states.

arc-b.verdict: Receipts are a ghostwriter's best tool for defending an edit to a client, and the Studio pricing card finally looks like a real tier, but the client story is the last tile of a pastel bento and the look is too loud to send to a CFO founder.
arc-b.loved: Two things. Studio gets the dark pricing card with a lime 'Start Studio' CTA, so it reads as a real plan, not an afterthought. And the three-client strip (Marcus 'Dry, short, no hype' / Amara / Jun, each with struck-through never-says, '9:10 AM Lisbon', 'Waiting for approval' vs 'Approved') lets me compare voices side by side.
problems: No agency signal until 'clients' in a subhead at about 3.2 screens; the Studio tile appears at about 4.4 screens as the sixth tile in 'The rest of the job, on one desk'.
Voices are shown only as descriptors ('Warm, plain, direct'). I never see one draft rewritten differently for two clients, which is the proof I need that voices won't bleed together.
Crushed heavy grotesk, lime highlighter and pastel tiles feel Gumroad-creator. I'd hesitate to put this in front of a Series B founder as 'the tool we use on your account'.
The review link tile ('Anyone with the link can comment. Only you can post.') sits apart from the client strip, so approvals and comments never connect.
arc-b.fix: Turn the client strip into a full-width section placed right after Receipts, showing one idea rewritten for two clients with each one's receipt. That proves distinct voices and gives me something to show clients to justify edits.

arc-a.verdict: Same honest three-client strip and 'Only you can post' review link as arc-b in the calmer dark brand, but the peeling-sticker hero reads as a toy and Studio is still buried in a bento.
arc-a.loved: The review-link tile next to the client strip: an editor note on exact words plus 'Anyone with the link can comment. Only you can post.' That one sentence answers my biggest client-account fear. The who-for line 'Three clients, three voices. None of them sound like you.' is the best agency copy in the round.
problems: First agency mention at about 4.3 screens and Studio at about 4.7, the last tile of the 'Then everything after the first line' grid. The nav has only a generic 'Who it's for'.
Amber stickers peeling off a full ultramarine stage are fun for a solo trader but gimmicky to show a client whose account I'm responsible for.
The Studio pricing card is the plain one beside a loud blue Pro card, so visually the page says 'buy Pro'.
Nothing on how client accounts are connected, team seats for my writers, or who can post. 'Only you can post' doesn't say whether 'you' means me, my writer or the client.
arc-a.fix: Promote 'Three clients, three voices. None of them sound like you.' to a section headline over the client strip, pull that strip out of the bento, and add a line on seats and roles (writer drafts, owner schedules, client approves by link).

awwwards-b.verdict: The most fitting metaphor for a ghostwriting shop (an editor's blue pencil), but it whispers the agency story in small italics and its pricing headline is about $12.
awwwards-b.loved: The client tabs (Priya / Marcus / Lena) with voice, struck-through never-says and 'America/New_York · 7:45 AM', plus the rubber 'APPROVED BY MARCUS' stamp. Approval as a physical sign-off is a metaphor my clients would get instantly.
problems: No route in from the top: the nav reads 'THE EDIT / HOW IT WORKS / THE DESK / PRICING'; the first agency mention is at about 3.9 screens and Studio at about 5.1, set in small italic body copy.
The pricing headline 'Start at $0. Stay for $12.' frames the whole offer around the solo plan, and Studio's unit is a tiny mono caps 'PER CLIENT VOICE A MONTH'.
No approval queue or review-link-to-approval flow; the stamp is decoration, not a status I can manage across 8 clients.
Handwritten 'that's fine' and the pencil prop are charming but precious; mono all-caps UI makes the product look less like an operations tool.
awwwards-b.fix: Add 'For ghostwriters' to the nav and make 'Every client keeps their own voice.' a full section with a queue across clients ('2 waiting on Priya, 1 on Marcus'). Change the pricing headline so it doesn't name $12 as the price.

pickWhy: It's the only design that tells an agency 'this is for you' on the first screen, and its client switcher shows the per-client approval queue, never-say lists and time zones I juggle today, in a calm dark UI my clients would trust. It needs Studio moved up and the 'six vs four clients' slip fixed.
combo: Use typefully-a's page, nav and client switcher, but replace its Studio panel with apple-b's app mock (review link, client comment, Approve in one frame), clearly labelled as the client approving. Add arc-a's 'Anyone with the link can comment. Only you can post.' and arc-b's dark, featured Studio pricing card.
notes: All five use the identical Studio pricing copy. None answers the three things I need to quote and onboard: (1) seats/roles for my writers and who can post on a client's account (how accounts connect, OAuth, revoke); (2) a worked quote, e.g. 8 voices = $144/mo yearly or $192 monthly, and whether I also need Pro; (3) whether the 500 auto-posts limit applies per voice or in total. None shows what the client sees when they open a review link. Measured position of the Studio block on desktop (1440x900): arc-a 4.7 screens, arc-b 4.4, awwwards-b 5.1, apple-b 5.2 (own section), typefully-a 7.0 (own section; 10.7 phone screens).
